subject: Post-call: long-context evaluation plan and next steps for ClarityHealth
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@clarityhealth.com>, Dr. Marcus Lee <mlee@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: long-context evaluation plan and next steps for ClarityHealth

Hi Asha / Marcus —

Thanks again for the productive time today. Quick recap and a pragmatic evaluation plan so we can validate model fit for your discharge-summary and longitudinal note consolidation use cases:

Summary of needs we heard
- Consolidate multi-visit notes (avg 6–10 encounters) into a single longitudinal summary for clinician review.
- Preserve timeline/order and critical entities (meds, allergies, problem list).
- Very low tolerance for hallucinated meds / false positives.
- PHI inside source docs; you indicated on-prem / VPC preferred for pilot.

Proposed pilot evaluation scope
- Narrow benchmark: 200 real notes (anonymized) + 20 synthetic edge cases for very long history (>40k chars). See attached clarity_sample_note_batch.csv (stub).
- Models to benchmark: Redwood-Open-13B-8k (baseline), Redwood-Inst-70B-32k (quantized-4bit candidate), and a trimmed 1-pass summarizer (Redwood-Slim-3B) for fast recalls.
- Tests: truncation behavior (prefix vs suffix preservation), entity recall (medication + problem list), timeline fidelity (relative ordering), and summarization fidelity (ROUGE + clinical-entity recall).
- Prompt sets and rubric: I uploaded seed prompt variants and an initial rubric to the Drive folder below.

Links / artifacts
- Benchmark tracker: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1benchmark_sheet_clarity
- Prompt set & rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/clarity_prompt_sets
- Eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/clarity-pilot

Attachments (stubs): clarity_sample_note_batch.csv; pilot_plan_v1.pdf

Initial timeline & next steps
1) Redwood runs an internal smoke bench on the 200-note set (2–3 business days) — owner: Redwood (Diego).
2) Deliver preliminary metrics + failure-mode examples (truncation & hallucination) — owner: Neha — ETA: +5 business days after smoke bench.
3) Technical deep-dive call to review failure cases and decide on model variant and quantization strategy — proposed: Tue 2027-05-18 10:00 AM PT.
4) If pilot looks good, follow-on: private deployment (VPC) and extended 2k-note eval.

Main open questions from our side
- What are your retention / audit log requirements? (SOC2, e-discovery windows)
- For the anonymized sample set, can you confirm PHI redaction level (token-level vs free-text removal)?

Please let me know if we missed anything. If that plan looks good, I'll kick off the smoke bench and share the test harness.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pilot_plan_v1.pdf)
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@clarityhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Marcus Lee <mlee@clarityhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: long-context evaluation plan and next steps for ClarityHealth

Thanks Diego — this captures the conversation well. A few clarifications and constraints from our security/compliance and clinical teams:

1) PHI & hosting — we require VPC with customer-managed KMS for the pilot (we cannot use hosted shared inference). On-prem is preferred if latency is a hard requirement.
2) Redaction — we'll provide two datasets: (a) token-redacted export for quick smoke tests and (b) limited-tokenized export for final fidelity checks. Both will be delivered via secure S3.
3) Hallucination tolerance — for meds and allergies we need >95% precision in automatic extraction; anything lower will require a conservative fallback (flag for clinician review).
4) Timeline — 200-note smoke bench OK; please surface representative failure examples (raw inputs + model output) so our clinicians can triage.

We also noted that long encounter chains sometimes have duplicated templated sections (e.g., repeated med lists) which tend to amplify truncation issues in the tail. We'd like the evaluation to include synthetic cases that intentionally replicate that template repetition.

Can Neha and Diego confirm whether you can run the smoke bench within our VPC or will we need a redwood-hosted run with encrypted payloads?

Thanks,
Asha
VP Product, ClarityHealth
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: long-context evaluation plan and next steps for ClarityHealth

Diego / Marissa — quick internal note to tighten the bench following Asha's constraints:

Proposed additions to test matrix (I attached a draft eval_matrix.xlsx stub):
- PHI-handling modes: run both token-redacted and limited-tokenized inputs to compare delta in entity recall.
- Template-repeat stress test: add 30 synthetic notes with repeated med lists and homepage templates to force truncation interactions.
- Prefix vs suffix truncation test: for models limited to 8k vs 32k windows, measure loss of earliest vs latest events and report timeline inversion rate.
- Regression criteria: set a hard regression gate for meds/allergy precision (>=95%). If a candidate model fails gate, propose fallback to the Slim-3B 'extract-and-flag' pipeline.
- Quantization checks: for Redwood-Inst-70B-32k we'll run both normal float and quantized-4bit to compare hallucination drift (we've seen shifts on verbatim copying in quantized runs).

Owner & ETA suggestions
- Diego: run initial smoke bench with token-redacted set (2 business days).
- Neha: run quantization comparison and aggregate metrics (5 business days after smoke bench).
- Marissa: coordinate docs + clinical review slots with Asha's team (she can own scheduling).

I'll add these rows to the spreadsheet and push to the Drive folder.

-Neha
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: eval_matrix.xlsx)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: long-context evaluation plan and next steps for ClarityHealth

Asha — great, thanks for the clarifications. Short answers and operational plan: 

1) VPC / hosting: we can run the smoke bench inside your VPC using our private agent; we'll need a short runbook and an S3 staging location. I'll send the onboarding checklist after you confirm the S3 path.
2) PHI redaction modes: confirmed — we'll run both token-redacted and limited-tokenized inputs as Neha outlined.
3) Hallucination gate: we'll instrument the harness to flag any med/allergy precision < 95% and produce per-document false-positive lists for clinician review.
4) Template-repeat tests: included — Neha will add the 30 synthetic repeats to the set.

Proposed meeting to review smoke bench outputs and decide pilot configuration:
- Tue 2027-05-18 10:00 AM PT (45 min) — Tech + Clinical review. Meeting link: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210

Immediate next actions
- ACTION (Diego): Kick off VPC onboarding checklist & request S3 path — by EOD Mon 2027-05-16.
- ACTION (Neha): Finalize eval_matrix and run quantization comparison after smoke bench — ETA: +5 business days after bench.
- ACTION (Marissa): Book clinical review slots with Asha's team for Wed/Thu next week.

HubSpot / procurement notes
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CLH-2027-04
- I'll also attach a one-page pilot SOW after the bench for legal review / DocuSign.

If that schedule works, we'll treat the Tue review as the decision point for model variant and deployment mode.

Thanks — and we'll wait for the S3 path to start the bench.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pilot_plan_v1.pdf)
